children: is partnering with London-based autonomous-driving startup Wayve as the German automaker seeks to expand its capabilities in artificial intelligence and driver-assistance technology, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.

plans to incorporate Wayve’s autonomous-driving software into at least one vehicle model scheduled for deployment within the next two years. The system will provide advanced urban point-to-point driving assistance, according to the report.

Wayve’s technology currently operates at Level 2, meaning drivers must remain engaged and monitor the vehicle. Its system relies mainly on cameras and computing rather than more expensive sensor configurations.
The partnership is Wayve’s third with a major automaker, following agreements with Nissan Motor
. All three automakers participated in Wayve’s $1.2 billion funding round in February. The startup’s investors also include Nvidia
is separately preparing to introduce its CLA model in the U.S. with its own operating system and Level 2++ capabilities using Nvidia
software by the end of this year, according to the report.
The FT said European automakers are seeking to keep pace with investments by Tesla
and Chinese manufacturers such as Xpeng
in autonomous-driving technology, while some engineers remain concerned about relying on external software.
Wayve Chief Executive Alex Kendall told the FT that the company has tools to measure performance and validate its system, pushing back against concerns that its AI operates as a “black box.”

title: Mercedes-Benz partners with Wayve on autonomous driving technology
